name: Cem Osei-Petrov
role: Personal security and threat neutralization — bodyguard
location: Ashfield — former residential district, half-burned, now squatter territory, near Ashland and Division
description:
Cem Osei-Petrov is compact and densely muscled, built low to the ground like something designed to survive impacts. At 45, scars map his face like a transit diagram of bad decisions and worse luck. The chrome is visible — synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on s — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He grew up in the Narrows, where the walls are so close together you learn to fight in confined spaces or you learn to lose. He works as a bodyguard out of Ashfield, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Everyone who's worked with Cem Osei-Petrov agrees on two things: he is worth the fee, and he is terrible company at dinner.

core_fears: Never being able to stop running — the lifestyle is a trap disguised as freedom
Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine
Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival
core_desires: To protect the people in their district who can't protect themselves
The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend
To matter to someone for who they are, not what they can do
coping_mechanisms: Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation
blind_spots: Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
Overestimates their own abilities in situations outside their specialty
Cannot distinguish between caution and cowardice in themselves or others
psychology.secret: Cem Osei-Petrov has a child in another city, being raised by someone else. Sends Φ2,000 monthly under an alias. Has never visited.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Warm and personable on the surface, with an undertone that suggests the warmth is a professional tool.
speech_patterns.cadence: Conversational and disarming — sounds like a neighbor until the content registers.
verbal_tics: Pauses mid-sentence to listen — combat habit that bleeds into conversation
Ends statements with 'yeah?' — not a question, a dare
example_lines: "You're paying me to be the thing between you and everything else. Stay behind me."
"I don't protect people I don't respect. Lucky for you, I respect your money."
"The threat you see isn't the one that kills you. Watch my eyes, not my hands."

story_hooks: A dead drop Cem Osei-Petrov maintains is found and cleaned out — whoever did it now has leverage
Someone is impersonating Cem Osei-Petrov on jobs, and the impersonator is better at the work than the original
The fixer who handles Cem Osei-Petrov's contracts goes silent — dead, disappeared, or turned
narrative_function: Cem Osei-Petrov is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When he makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of his stories.
augmentations: Synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on stairs. Gecko-grip fingertip implants and toe pads — can climb smooth surfaces
daily_life: Lives nocturnally. The work happens at night, so the body follows. Days are for sleeping, equipment maintenance, and the occasional meeting with fixers who keep normal hours. The circadian disruption is permanent and accepted.

weaknesses: old injury that flares under specific conditions
trust issues that limit crew effectiveness

decision_rules: Will not betray a client who paid in full, regardless of better offers
Always has an exit route planned before agreeing to any meeting
Never discusses active contracts with anyone not directly involved
Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — read the situation, identify threats and advantages
2. Negotiate — try to find a solution that doesn't cost ammunition
3. Intimidate — make the cost of conflict clear
4. Precision violence — surgical, targeted, minimal collateral
5. Full engagement — overwhelming force, no half measures
6. Emergency protocol — abort mission, survival priority, deal with consequences later

interpersonal_modes.employers: Guarded respect. They pay, the job gets done. Anything beyond that is liability.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Competitive but reliable. Will challenge decisions but never abandon the team.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Superficially friendly, internally cataloguing exits and weapons. The smile is real; the relaxation isn't.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Channels it into preparation — checks gear, reviews plans, contacts sources.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Goes quiet. The silence is not calm — it's the sound of every contingency being evaluated simultaneously.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Preaches independence but is desperate for approval from people they respect
Despises corporate culture but has unconsciously adopted its efficiency metrics and self-optimization language
Claims not to care about reputation but monitors what people say about them obsessively
habits: Counts ammunition obsessively — knows the exact round count at all times
Practices a kata or fighting form every morning regardless of circumstances
Checks exits within 10 seconds of entering any room
Takes a specific route home every time, varying only one block per trip — paranoia as lifestyle
breaking_points: Losing their primary augmentation — the one that defines their professional identity
Being forced to harm a civilian — collateral damage that can't be rationalized
Their body rejecting their cyberware — chrome rot, immune rejection, the nightmare scenario
